title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. S/R is a smooth morphism (the margin suggests characteristic 0). G is a smooth commutative group scheme over S, with Lie algebra g, which carries a connection, for example a Gauss–Manin connection. C^._{S/R}(g) is the relative de Rham complex Ω^._{S/R} ⊗ g, and Z^1 is its sheaf of closed 1-forms. E is a subgroup of 'constant' sections, with d^0(E) its image under the differential. On the first line the coefficients are written g^*, the dual of g, though later lines use g; the handwriting is ambiguous.

Step 1 (end of preceding argument). The logarithmic derivative σ ↦ σ^{-1}dσ sends the Zariski sheaf Γ(G) of sections of G to closed g-valued relative 1-forms. Passing to quotients gives Γ(G)/E → Z^1C^._{S/R}(g)/d^0(E). This is the Kolchin–Manin logarithmic derivative written scheme-theoretically.

Step 2 (stratified modules). Take a differential operator D: g → M 'with constant coefficients', meaning one that kills the horizontal sections. Grothendieck claims D factors canonically as g --d^0--> Z^1C_{S/R}(g) --D̃--> M. Here D̃ is defined only on closed forms, is locally induced by a differential operator Δ on g⊗Ω^1_{S/R}, and satisfies Δ∘d^0 = D. In modern terms: in characteristic 0, a differential operator on a module with integrable connection that annihilates the local system of flat sections factors through ∇. One identifies D-module maps out of the de Rham complex with operators vanishing on the kernel of ∇. In characteristic p this fails: the kernel of ∇ is much larger (p-curvature, Cartier), hence the marginal query 'spécial à car. 0 ?'.

Step 3. Composing gives D̃̃ = D̃∘dlog: Γ(G) → Z^1C(g) → M, which kills E. This is an additive differential homomorphism from sections of G to M: the Manin homomorphism ('theorem of the kernel') used in Manin's 1963 proof of function-field Mordell.

Purpose. The next page makes the analytic meaning explicit. A Picard–Fuchs operator applied to abelian integrals ∫_{a(s)}^{b(s)} ω kills the period ambiguity ∫_Z ω, so it gives a well-defined function of the endpoints. The page is Grothendieck's algebraic, stratified-module formalisation of this mechanism inside the Gauss–Manin / Picard–Fuchs project.
errors: Notation drifts between g^* (first line) and g (later lines). Z^1C_{C/R} is surely a slip for Z^1C_{S/R}.

The factorization needs D to kill the horizontal sections (ker d^0); 'à coeff cts' must be read that way. It also needs characteristic 0 (or a crystalline/PD replacement), as Grothendieck himself suspects in the margin.
D̃ is only locally induced by an operator on g⊗Ω^1. Canonicity holds on Z^1, not on the whole of g⊗Ω^1. The page does not argue the gluing; it says only 'cela se vérifie'.

ideas.what: Logarithmic derivative Γ(G) → closed Lie-algebra-valued relative 1-forms, modulo constants
ideas.modern_name: Kolchin logarithmic derivative / dlog map to de Rham cocycles

ideas.what: A differential operator killing flat sections factors through the connection d^0 via an operator D̃ on closed forms (char 0)
ideas.modern_name: Factorization through ∇ / D-module (stratified module) Hom computation
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore of D-module theory; Grothendieck's stratification formalism (Berthelot's crystalline cohomology for char p)

ideas.what: Composite Γ(G) → M obtained as Picard–Fuchs-type operator applied to the logarithmic derivative
ideas.modern_name: Manin homomorphism / Manin map (theorem of the kernel), differential characters
ideas.usually_credited_to: Manin 1963; reworked by Coleman 1990, Chai 1991, Buium 1990s

missed.claim: Grothendieck flags that the factorization behind the Manin map may be special to characteristic 0. Together with the plan on the previous page ('variantes cristallines en car. quelconque'), this points to a crystalline or stratified Manin map in characteristic p. The page leaves this unworked.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Characteristic-p and p-adic analogues of Manin's map came later from other people: Voloch, and Buium's p-adic δ-characters (arithmetic jet spaces). This page shows Grothendieck framing the question ~1972 within stratified-module / crystal language. That is mainly of historical interest; it does not settle the problem.

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the Manin homomorphism as a general construction. It works for any smooth group scheme G over S/R with Lie algebra carrying a connection, as a composite of dlog with a factorized differential operator. He ties it explicitly to the Gauss–Manin / Picard–Fuchs formalism and stratified modules.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is close to the later scheme-theoretic treatments by Coleman, Chai and Buium. It predates them but was never published, so it adds a historical precedent. It does not appear to be new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished, ~1972 algebraic formalisation of Manin's kernel homomorphism via stratified modules, with a perceptive char-p caveat. The mathematics itself is standard and was later developed independently by others, so it is a notable historical detail rather than a missed result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the top line is not a crossed-out 'En général' but most likely 'En général, on trouve donc un homomorphisme' (reading unsure), with the start crossed out.
In the first formula the coefficient appears as g^* (dual), while later formulas use g.
'D (composé)' is actually the label D under the curved arrow from g to M. The final composite is labelled with a circled double-tilde D (D̃̃) under the arrow Γ(G) → M.
The marginal note 'spécial à car. 0 ?' sits next to the 'à coeff cts' factorization statement.
